subject: Post-call: renewal step-up scenarios, blended pricing & route add proposal
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kate Thomas <kate@cambridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: renewal step-up scenarios, blended pricing & route add proposal

Thanks again for the time this morning, Kate — good conversation. Quick recap + asks so we can get a concrete proposal to your procurement team before next week.

Call summary (short):
- Current production: ~2.9M tokens/month (inference + some embedding usage).
- Expected step-up: planning scenarios show 8–12M tokens/month on a 3–6 month ramp if the pilot hits its KPIs.
- Priority workloads: chat/assistant (low latency) for patient-facing flows, and nightly batch embedding jobs for analytics.

Cost/target guidance we discussed:
- Your stated budget window: roughly $7k–$12k/month for steady-state (this matches the internal numbers you showed).
- You asked for a target $/1M tokens number to take into budgeting. Based on scale and mixed routes we discussed, an initial goalpost we can aim for is $850–900 per 1M tokens at scale (after blended discounts).

Suggested pricing structure to evaluate (illustrative):
- 0–2M/month: $1,200 per 1M tokens (standard hosted, no commitment).
- 2–10M/month: $900 per 1M tokens (blended committed band).
- >10M/month: $750 per 1M tokens (high-volume blended band or Dedicated reserve).
- Add-on: embeddings route as a separate line item (custom unit price when routed to optimized embedding model).

Routing/architecture notes:
- Recommend a two-route approach: FAST (low-latency dev/synchronous calls) and ECON (batch or async embedding/analytics). We can map 65–80% of traffic to FAST for the pilot and route heavy analytics to ECON.
- If you want hard latency SLOs for the FAST route we should evaluate dedicated capacity; otherwise hosted with KV-caching + batching gives comparable economics for many flows.

Action items / next steps (for clarity):
1) Kate/Procurement: confirm the budget target you want me to include in the formal proposal — is $850 per 1M tokens acceptable as the target to test with finance?
2) Cambridge: share a small sample of a week of traffic (anonymized) and any peak QPS numbers so we can model tail latency and burst capacity.
3) Redwood: we will produce a short proposal (pricing bands, ramp schedule options, and a 30–60 day bridge credit option) + an updated draft SOW that calls out route splits and embedding as a separate billable item.

Attachments: CH-usage-sample.csv (sample traffic), redwood-stepup-playbook.pdf (how we model blends and routes).

Thanks — aiming to get the draft in front of your team by EOD Thursday.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0198

[Attachment: CH-usage-sample.csv (csv, 48KB)]
[Attachment: redwood-stepup-playbook.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)]
From: Kate Thomas <kate@cambridgehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurements@cambridgehealth.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: renewal step-up scenarios, blended pricing & route add proposal

Thanks Ben — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Current baseline is 3.1M tokens/month (we double-checked logs). The 8–12M ramp is accurate as a target if the pilot succeeds; finance will likely model 10M avg for Q1 as a conservative plan.
- For budgeting, we prefer to carry a single target rate in the model. Our internal ask: can you aim to present a target of $850 per 1M tokens (blended) for the board deck? That’s what finance prefers to see.
- About routing: yes, we will want the FAST route to have an uptime/latency SLO since it's customer-facing. If dedicated capacity is required for that SLO, flag it in the proposal along with incremental monthly cost.
- For bridge credit: procurement likes a short 30-day ramp credit (not more than 30%) while we confirm integration stability. Can you bake a 30% first-month credit into the proposal as an option?

I will share an anonymized week of traffic by EOD today (sending to your shared folder). Also copying procurement on timeline.

—Kate
Kate Thomas
Director of Product — Cambridge Health
kate@cambridgehealth.com

On Tue, Sep 7, 2027 at 09:12 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the time this morning, Kate — good conversation. Quick recap + asks so we can get a concrete proposal to your procurement team before next week.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: renewal step-up scenarios, blended pricing & route add proposal

Looping in pricing notes from renewal desk — quick thoughts to include in the draft:

- If Cambridge can commit to ~9M avg tokens/month over a 12-month period we can put forward $850 per 1M as the target blended rate (confirming their request). We should call out the commit bands explicitly: 0–2M, 2–9M, 9–20M with step discounts.
- Recommend a 60-day review clause for the first three months to adjust banding if actual usage diverges >25%. Keeps both sides protected.
- First-month ramp credit: we can offer 30% credit capped at the first $10k of bill for the initial month (this meets procurement ask for a short bridge but protects revenue).
- Embeddings: charge separately (we usually quote embeddings at a 30–40% premium to the same token band if routed to an embedding-optimized model), or offer a packaged discount if they commit to a separate embeddings band. Call out as line-item so procurement can code budget lines correctly.
- Legal: they asked about SLOs for FAST route. Flagging that any hard SLO >99.9% may require Dedicated capacity or a premium SLA add-on; we'll mark both options in the SOW.

Action for Ben: include these three things in the proposal: the 12-month commit band pricing table, the 60-day review clause, and the capped 30% first-month credit. Also add an explicit line for embeddings and a separate routing appendix.

Marissa
Director, Renewal Desk | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kate Thomas <kate@cambridgehealth.com>, procurements@cambridgehealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Sep 2027 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: Updated: Proposal draft + next steps (DocuSign link & meeting invite)

Kate — thanks for the quick turnaround on the sample traffic (received and reviewed). Appreciate procurement jumping in.

Per our internal alignment, attached is a short draft proposal (proposal-draft-CH.docx) showing:
- Commit bands: 0–2M ($1,200/1M), 2–9M ($900/1M), 9–20M ($850/1M).
- A 12-month term that targets a 9M average to qualify for the $850 blended rate.
- 60-day review clause for banding adjustment if usage varies by +/-25% for rolling months 1–3.
- First-month credit option: 30% credit capped at $10k (checkbox in the SOW).
- Embeddings line-item and routing appendix to define FAST vs ECON.

Links: HubSpot deal record (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/CH-98765) and an optional DocuSign template we've prepared (https://www.docusign.com/prepare/CH-DEAL-2027).

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick contract review meeting — I propose Monday 9/13, 10:00–10:30am PT. I’ve sent a calendar invite.
2) If legal/procurement approve, we'll send a DocuSign version with the selected credit checkbox and the agreed commit band.
3) Technical kick-off: 2-week PoC plan (configure route split, smoke tests, and a performance baseline).

If the $850 per 1M blended target is acceptable to finance, we can lock that into the proposal subject to the commit band. Otherwise let me know what number your board needs and we can re-run options (we have flexibility in the >9M band if they can expand the term).

Attaching: proposal-draft-CH.docx (word draft).

Best,
Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
